August 31 – September 6, 2026 · Airbnb APAC leadership briefing

🎙️ Listen to this issue

Akira & Sera · 6 min 25 sec · August 31–September 6, 2026

Download audio · Subscribe via RSS

The week in one line: Shorter, higher-quality trips and regional access shifts favour precise corridor execution—not a blanket bet on Asian travel growth.

🔥 Key Signals

Shorter trips do not necessarily mean cheaper stays. Hotels.com says two-to-three-night trips account for about 60% of Chuseok searches, versus roughly 50% last year, while upscale properties exceed 60% of searched nights. Separately, Trip.com reports almost half of Malaysian overseas hotel bookings in four- and five-star accommodation. These are distinct platform samples, not a regional average: the common mechanism is concentrating available time and spend into fewer, higher-quality nights. 한국경제 / Hotels.com · 2026-08-31The Rakyat Post / Trip.com platform data · 2026-09-04
Regional access is changing the accommodation catchment. Gimhae marginally overtook Incheon as the entry point for Taiwanese visitors in July, with shares of 36.9% and 36.3%. New Kobe–Incheon service and restored Kitakyushu–Taipei flights add options outside familiar gateways. This makes neighbourhood readiness commercially relevant, but flights can carry residents and connecting passengers: capacity creates an opportunity to compete for nights, not proof of additional Airbnb demand. 뉴스트래블 citing Korea Tourism Organization Taipei office · 2026-09-02TRAICY · 2026-09-01TRAICY Global · 2026-09-02
Autumn demand and transport supply are not moving in lockstep. China’s holiday-window domestic air bookings were reported up about 17% year on year, while OAG puts September Indian seats down 4.5%. Within Southeast Asia, Vietnam’s departing capacity rises 10%, but Malaysia and the Philippines contract. Timing and geography matter more than a generic recovery narrative. Strong platform spending can coexist with tighter seats and higher trip costs; monthly schedules are forward supply, not realised passenger traffic. 新浪新闻（转载第一财经、界面等） · 2026-09-05OAG · 2026-09-03OAG · 2026-09-03
Platforms are competing on the total trip, including constraints. Japan’s hotel, package and airline promotions overlap, while Air India–IHG links flight loyalty with hotel stays. Fujiyoshida’s Uber partnership instead tackles pickup locations and visitor conduct. Price, rewards and on-the-ground certainty all influence conversion. Airbnb should distinguish the mechanism before responding: a coupon needs a value comparison; congestion needs operational guidance; a reported visa change needs accurate eligibility information rather than an indiscriminate discount. Rakuten Group · 2026-09-01 Uber Japan · 2026-09-04 Travel Watch · 2026-09-01Travel Trade Journal · 2026-09-04

💡 Airbnb APAC Implications

Build short-break value around the whole group. Test two-to-three-night, easy-arrival homes for Korea-origin autumn trips, showing total group cost and specific comforts rather than claiming that homes are automatically cheaper than premium hotels. Measure conversion, cancellation and total paid per guest against comparable stays. The search evidence supports a hypothesis about compressed trips and quality, not a licence to forecast Airbnb bookings. 한국경제 / Hotels.com · 2026-08-31 호텔앤레스토랑 / HotelsCombined · 2026-09-04
Prioritise a small set of regional corridors, not blanket expansion. Review legally eligible supply, language coverage, self check-in and airport instructions around Busan, Kobe and northern Kyushu. Route-specific demand should decide where acquisition investment follows. Separate guest origin, airport entry and final destination in analysis; a gateway share shift alone cannot identify the neighbourhoods where incremental stays will land. 뉴스트래블 citing Korea Tourism Organization Taipei office · 2026-09-02TRAICY · 2026-09-01TRAICY Global · 2026-09-02
Translate China’s domestic behaviour into outbound hypotheses only. Meituan’s family stays and Fliggy’s room-night growth describe domestic activity. Airbnb’s relevant commercial question is whether China-origin guests carry those preferences into Japan and Southeast Asia: group space, slower itineraries and local experiences. Validate with outbound funnel and stay-length data before reallocating spend. Do not describe Chinese domestic accommodation figures as Airbnb’s addressable domestic business. 新华网 / 美团数据 · 2026-09-03 新华网 · 2026-08-31
Protect long-stay clarity and event-period trust. Reports say Thailand’s visa-exempt allowance falls to 30 days from September 15 for affected passports. Verify current official entry rules before guest-facing guidance and distinguish immigration permission from accommodation legality. Delhi’s summit pricing separately calls for transparent totals and dependable host calendars. Neither a policy headline nor hotel scarcity justifies promising unrestricted stays or assuming displaced delegates will choose homes. The Straits Times / The Nation Asia News Network · 2026-09-02The Hindu BusinessLine · 2026-09-04

🏢 Competitor & Platform Watch

Rakuten and Yahoo sharpen the effective-price comparison. Rakuten’s domestic campaign advertises more than 20,000 lodging offers and up to 35% off first app bookings; Yahoo’s packages advertise coupons up to ¥30,000 and PayPay rewards. Korea-facing Rakuten offers have different dates and eligibility. These are maximum promotional terms, not realised savings or market-wide price falls. Monitor eligible basket prices and the friction of redeeming rewards, rather than comparing headline discounts. Rakuten Group · 2026-09-01 Travel Watch · 2026-09-01BusinessKorea / Rakuten Travel Korea · 2026-09-02
Scapia and Air India–IHG aim to capture the next booking. The Axis–Scapia card combines zero forex markup with up to 20% Scapia Coins on eligible bookings. Air India–IHG offers triple Maharaja Points on qualifying stays from September 15 through December 31. Both attach retention to transactions beyond the room search. Redemption rules and traveller overlap will determine their impact; neither announcement demonstrates a share shift away from Airbnb. ETTravelWorld · 2026-09-04 Travel Trade Journal · 2026-09-04
KATA’s committee is an early policy signal, not a new law. The Korean trade association’s standing fair-cooperation committee brings foreign-OTA conduct, registration parity and consumer protection onto its agenda. That could shape consultation and enforcement priorities, but the collected record does not establish enacted obligations. Maintain a watch on concrete proposals and local supplier responsibilities; distinguish industry advocacy from government decisions when briefing hosts or leadership. TTL뉴스 / Korea Association of Travel Agents · 2026-08-31
Klook and Uber show two forms of destination partnership. The Philippine tourism department’s MOU with Klook and Newport World Resorts concerns domestic and entertainment promotion; Uber’s Fujiyoshida agreement specifies pickup guidance, local rules and congestion information. The former is a distribution commitment, the latter an operating intervention. Neither includes measured outcomes in this pool. Airbnb should evaluate partnerships against incremental nights and neighbourhood friction, not announcement volume. Philippine News Agency · 2026-09-01Uber Japan · 2026-09-04

🇮🇳 India (भारत)

Executive summary
  • Event pressure is concentrated, not nationwide. BusinessLine cites Delhi five-star searches up 50% and hotel bookings up 25% year on year around BRICS. Treat the premium-city spike as a dated occasion, not a national accommodation growth rate. The Hindu BusinessLine · 2026-09-04
  • Domestic demand is drawing branded supply outward. Mint describes chains entering smaller destinations; Hilton reports 60 hotels under construction and commitments for another 400. Those pipeline stages are not equivalent to rooms available today, but they raise the future competitive bar. Mint · 2026-09-01 Business Standard · 2026-09-03
  • Outbound substitution meets constrained air supply. Industry commentary points travellers toward shorter, more affordable regional trips, while OAG’s September schedule totals 22.7 million seats, down 4.5% year on year. New routes do not negate a contracting national total. The Economic Times · 2026-09-04 OAG · 2026-09-03
Supporting detail
Inbound recovery remains a separate problem. FAITH’s 8–9 million foreign-visitor outlook is an industry forecast reported by Economic Times, not a final arrivals count. It sits alongside robust domestic investment rather than contradicting it. Keep inbound and domestic assumptions separate when sizing destination opportunities; neither foreign-arrival weakness nor hotel construction alone settles home demand. The Economic Times · 2026-09-06
Central Asia gains both access and distribution. The Uzbekistan visa-free announcement and Centrum Air’s planned twice-weekly Hyderabad–Tashkent launch on September 28 remove different frictions: permission and nonstop access. Air India’s Ahmedabad Easy Connect instead improves transfers to 26 international destinations through Delhi. These are corridor-specific changes, not evidence that every outbound segment is accelerating. Travel Trade Journal · 2026-09-02 ETTravelWorld · 2026-08-31 Travel Trade Journal · 2026-09-01
Loyalty makes the accommodation choice less independent. Scapia’s travel rewards and Air India–IHG’s cross-loyalty offer can influence where a traveller starts the next booking. Airbnb should compare the complete value proposition for families and groups while watching actual redemption and retention. Announced benefits establish competitive intent; the collection contains no adoption data or measured effect on accommodation market share. ETTravelWorld · 2026-09-04 Travel Trade Journal · 2026-09-04

🇰🇷 Korea (대한민국)

Executive summary
  • Chuseok planning favours compact, comfortable breaks. Hotels.com’s search mix puts roughly 60% of trips at two or three nights and more than 60% of searched nights in four- and five-star properties. Search intentions remain upstream of completed stays. 한국경제 / Hotels.com · 2026-08-31
  • Outbound interest is rising within a second platform sample. HotelsCombined reports overseas hotel searches increasing from 37% to 60% of its holiday mix. That is a share change, not 60% growth, and must not be merged with Hotels.com into one dataset. 호텔앤레스토랑 / HotelsCombined · 2026-09-04
  • Busan is gaining Taiwan-facing gateway relevance. Gimhae handled 36.9% of July Taiwanese arrivals, just above Incheon’s 36.3%. The reported 900 Taipei–Gimhae flights help explain access, but visitor destination and length of stay still need validation. 뉴스트래블 citing Korea Tourism Organization Taipei office · 2026-09-02
Supporting detail
Aviation depth and Japan promotions reinforce one corridor. September schedule reporting highlights Incheon–Narita’s international seat ranking, while Rakuten markets Japan lodging discounts to Korean customers. Availability and promotion can reduce trip-planning friction together. The commercial question is conversion into a short, reliable itinerary; neither a route ranking nor a maximum coupon measures the demand captured by independent accommodation. 항공여행 · 2026-09-02 BusinessKorea / Rakuten Travel Korea · 2026-09-02
Workation is product positioning, not proof of a boom. KTO’s English-language guide presents communities, remote-work appeal and visa options. That supports checking workspace quality, connectivity and longer-stay readiness in eligible homes. It does not demonstrate a new visa rule this week or quantify remote-worker arrivals. Avoid presenting promotional destination content as either enacted reform or observed growth. VISITKOREA / Korea Tourism Organization · 2026-09-02
Platform-policy advocacy deserves a concrete watchlist. KATA’s committee raises registration and consumer-protection parity, alongside inbound guide qualifications. Follow published proposals and enforcement decisions rather than extrapolating a ban or opening from a trade-association launch. The missing official policy release and unavailable Naver backup constrain confidence about the complete regulatory picture this week. TTL뉴스 / Korea Association of Travel Agents · 2026-08-31

🇯🇵 Japan (日本)

Executive summary
  • Autumn planning is an active competitive battleground. Rakuten’s 28-day sale and Yahoo’s air-plus-hotel promotion target the booking window with different mechanics. Compare eligible total prices, not advertised ceilings; promotions alone do not prove weak demand. Rakuten Group · 2026-09-01 Travel Watch · 2026-09-01
  • New gateways widen options around Kansai. Asiana launched daily Kobe–Incheon service on September 1, scheduled through March 27, 2027. It adds Korean access and network connections, but additional seats are not yet evidence of additional local overnight stays. TRAICY · 2026-09-01
  • Visitor-flow management is becoming a platform function. Uber and Fujiyoshida will use designated pickup guidance, etiquette messaging and restriction information around Fuji tourism areas. The practical implication is better arrival coordination, not an assumption that congestion is already solved. Uber Japan · 2026-09-04
Supporting detail
Hotel assets are being repackaged for drive tourism. Ooedo-Onsen Monogatari opened reservation-only RV stays at seven properties from ¥3,500 per vehicle-night, using existing bathing, dining and staffed facilities. This competes through predictable amenities rather than conventional room inventory. Airbnb can learn from the clarity of the proposition without inferring a measured camper-demand surge from one operator’s launch. Travel Watch · 2026-09-03
Fare sales and local incentives lower different barriers. Peach’s sale offers selected one-way fares from ¥4,000 for travel beginning September 28, while regional campaigns and Gifu lodging-only hometown-tax coupons reduce costs at destination. Eligibility and availability vary. Connecting suitable homes to accessible regional itineraries is a testable idea; aggregating these offers into a nationwide subsidy or average saving would be misleading. Travel Watch · 2026-09-02 Travel Watch · 2026-09-04 Nippon Air Transport via PR Times · 2026-09-04
Seasonality needs evidence beyond campaign calendars. Nikkei describes heat and foreign visitors shifting peak earnings toward autumn, but its original page was unavailable to the collector. Use that as a directional interpretation alongside verified promotions, not a quantified forecast. Trip.com’s forthcoming Tourism EXPO presence adds trade visibility; it provides no independent consumer demand or booking-performance measure. Nikkei Asia · 2026-09-02 Trip.com International Travel Japan via PR Times · 2026-09-03

🇨🇳 China (中国)

Executive summary
  • Family travel is leaning into time at destination. Meituan’s summer observation, reported by Xinhua, identifies four-to-five-day stays as common among families and rising county-level interest. These are platform observations about domestic behaviour, not a representative national stay-length estimate. 新华网 / 美团数据 · 2026-09-03
  • Fliggy reports substantial domestic room-night growth. The platform says summer hotel room nights rose 66% year on year and attraction tickets nearly 30%. Platform scope and season matter: do not translate this into national hotel growth or Airbnb performance. 新华网 · 2026-08-31
  • Cheap shoulder-season fares coexist with holiday advance demand. Reported September 25–October 7 air bookings exceed 3.83 million domestic and 1.77 million cross-border tickets, up about 17% and 11%. Those are booking snapshots as of September 4, not final passenger totals. 新浪新闻（转载第一财经、界面等） · 2026-09-05
Supporting detail
Summer aviation provides scale, with different denominators. The 62-day transport season recorded 151 million civil-aviation passenger journeys. A separate July 1–August 25 window counted over 7.06 million inbound-route passengers. Neither is a count of unique tourists, and inbound-route passengers need not all be foreign visitors. Their useful role is contextualising access and seasonal concentration, not sizing Airbnb bookings. 新华网 / 航旅纵横 · 2026-09-03
Shanghai is adding reasons to visit in autumn. The tourism festival’s programme includes more than 170 cultural and tourism activities across food, night visits and slower exploration. The mechanism is occasion-led itinerary formation; the release does not quantify incremental nights. For China-origin outbound merchandising, use the preference for participation as a hypothesis, while keeping Shanghai’s domestic programme outside direct Airbnb inventory claims. 新华社 · 2026-09-04
Forward hotel interest is not the same as realised occupancy. Qunar’s reported popular-city holiday advance bookings rise nearly 40%, alongside a 21% increase in interest in booking air travel a month ahead. These measures support monitoring lead times and price sensitivity, but cannot be added to Fliggy room nights or national passenger counts. The Tianjin expo is a supply-side industry event, not additional consumer demand evidence. 北京日报客户端 · 2026-08-31 新华丝路 · 2026-09-04

🌴 Southeast Asia

Executive summary
  • Vietnam leads the selected capacity comparison. OAG’s September departing seats rise 10% to 7.3 million, while Singapore rises 3.4% to 3.7 million. Malaysia and the Philippines decline 6.5% and 5.7%; this is an uneven supply outlook, not one regional recovery rate. OAG · 2026-09-03
  • Malaysia’s platform spending signal is strong but selective. Trip.com reports triple-digit H1 growth in flight and hotel spending and nearly quadrupled attraction bookings. A platform’s expansion and customer mix can amplify growth; these figures do not establish equivalent nationwide tourism spending gains. The Rakyat Post / Trip.com platform data · 2026-09-04
  • Thailand’s reported stay-limit change matters most for longer trips. The September 15 reduction from 60 to 30 visa-exempt days affects specified passports, including Singapore and Malaysia. Typical short breaks and longer stays face different exposure; official rules must be checked before traveller guidance. The Straits Times / The Nation Asia News Network · 2026-09-02
Supporting detail
Vietnam combines a holiday pulse with new connectivity. VNAT-attributed reporting estimates 6.5 million tourists over the August 29–September 2 National Day holiday, up 18.1%. Tourism Malaysia separately confirms daily Phu Quoc–Kuala Lumpur service from September 1. The former is an observed holiday estimate; the latter an access change. Test whether corridor demand supports suitable local stays rather than treating both as additive visitors. VietnamPlus (Vietnam News Agency), citing VNAT · 2026-09-03 Tourism Malaysia · 2026-09-01
Philippine operators are adapting to affordability pressure. PHILTOA describes a shift toward lower-cost land packages and nearby ASEAN markets as airfares rise. DOT’s 6.4–6.8 million arrivals goal, with seven million as a stretch, remains a target rather than achieved performance. Limited original-page extraction means the briefing cannot quantify the substitution or identify winners beyond the retained excerpts. Context.ph, citing Philippines Department of Tourism · 2026-09-01 Context.ph, citing PHILTOA · 2026-09-05
Activities distribution is expanding through partnerships. DOT’s Klook and Newport World Resorts MOU links domestic and entertainment promotion, while Travel Mart provides a consumer and trade activation. Both can help turn occasions into bookable products, but the source pool has no conversion results. Singapore-specific evidence is especially thin beyond schedules and Thailand policy; do not generalise Malaysian platform behaviour to Singapore. Philippine News Agency · 2026-09-01 Discover MNL / PHILTOA · 2026-09-03

🇭🇰🇹🇼 Hong Kong & Taiwan

Executive summary
  • Hong Kong gets a narrow new Mainland feeder. Hong Kong Airlines’ twice-weekly Urumqi service launched August 29 and was reported September 1. It adds a northwest-China connection and potential hub transfers; the record does not identify incremental Hong Kong overnight visitors. TRAICY Global · 2026-09-01
  • Premium cross-border mobility is being reshaped. EAA suspended most scheduled helicopter services from September 1, retaining Macau–Shenzhen scheduled flights and shifting other activity to charters. The operator cites heliport relocation and market changes, not a measured collapse in regional tourism. HK01 · 2026-09-02
  • Taiwan’s Japan access is rebuilding selectively. StarFlyer resumed Kitakyushu–Taoyuan on September 2 with three weekly round trips after a March 2020 suspension. Future frequency expansion is an ambition while demand is tested, not a committed capacity total. TRAICY Global · 2026-09-02
Supporting detail
Taiwan is targeting Malaysia through repeat and group travel. Coverage of the Tourism Administration’s MATTA Fair activity describes repeat-visitor and MICE/accommodation incentives, plus a Malaysia Airlines MOU for product development and joint marketing. The mechanism is coordinated source-market activation. The retained report is a secondary lifestyle/trade account, not an official terms document; do not promise incentive amounts, eligibility or measured uptake from it. Malaysian Foodie · 2026-09-05
Separate new access from the case for new supply. The Urumqi and northern-Kyushu routes connect distinct traveller pools and operate at modest frequencies. Review existing legal listing availability and transport guidance before inferring a need to acquire broadly across either market. Resident travel, connections and business trips may absorb seats without creating the same independent-accommodation demand as leisure overnight visitors. TRAICY Global · 2026-09-01 TRAICY Global · 2026-09-02
The evidence supports a corridor watch, not a market forecast. Four dated records meet the numerical richness floor, but three concern aviation and the fourth promotion. There is no retained direct consumer-search or booking series, and no first-party Taiwan incentive publication. Keep this section deliberately bounded: monitor destination-level nights and programme terms before claiming broad growth, price strength or an Airbnb share opportunity. HK01 · 2026-09-02 Malaysian Foodie · 2026-09-05

📅 Upcoming Travel Windows

September planning checkpoints. September 10–12: IATO convention in Visakhapatnam. September 15: reported Thailand entry-rule change and start of Air India–IHG promotional stays. September 24–27: Chuseok search window and Tourism EXPO Japan. September 28: planned Hyderabad–Tashkent launch and beginning of Peach’s eligible travel period. These are sourced commercial and planning dates, not a complete public-holiday calendar. 📋 Sources Audit

Verified input coverage: 6/6; shared upstream failure: none. Gate-approved dated records: India 20; Korea 9; Japan 10; China 7; Southeast Asia 10; Hong Kong/Taiwan 4; total 60. These are collection records, not 60 independent studies: India has two entries from one Aviation Week URL (59 distinct URLs overall), two Delhi stories covering the same event, and Rakuten coverage overlaps across markets. China has ten raw candidates but only seven gate-approved records; the other three are not used here.

Coverage is publication August 31–September 6, 2026; observation periods can be earlier or future. All six markets reach four dated records, but HK/TW only just does. Evidence volume does not remove selection bias. Search metadata can establish the recorded date without supplying a complete article. Company claims, forecasts, schedules, searches, journeys and completed stays are explicitly distinguished.

Material gaps. India’s claimed 20-item pool is not 20 independent events; its first-party train availability page is operational, not consumer demand, and is not used as a growth signal. The collection’s category/gap counts are internally inconsistent and are not repeated as validated quality metrics. Korea lacks an official policy release and its Naver backup was unavailable. Japan is promotion-heavy, with no new JNTO arrivals release or direct consumer dataset; Nikkei’s original-page DNS failure limits its use. China lacks independent hotel-company announcements and relies heavily on Xinhua platform reporting. SEA has thin Singapore-specific evidence and some blocked/incomplete original pages; Vietnam’s inconsistent cumulative-arrivals period is omitted. HK/TW lacks consumer data and official Taiwan incentive terms; its secondary programme account receives lower weight. The Korea fireworks guide is listed below but not used to assert an event date because event-date wording is weaker than publication evidence.

🌏 Asia Travel Weekly

August 31 – September 6, 2026 · Airbnb APAC leadership briefing

🎙️ Listen to this issue

Akira & Sera · 6 min 25 sec · August 31–September 6, 2026

Download audio · Subscribe via RSS

The week in one line: Shorter, higher-quality trips and regional access shifts favour precise corridor execution—not a blanket bet on Asian travel growth.

🔥 Key Signals

Shorter trips do not necessarily mean cheaper stays. Hotels.com says two-to-three-night trips account for about 60% of Chuseok searches, versus roughly 50% last year, while upscale properties exceed 60% of searched nights. Separately, Trip.com reports almost half of Malaysian overseas hotel bookings in four- and five-star accommodation. These are distinct platform samples, not a regional average: the common mechanism is concentrating available time and spend into fewer, higher-quality nights. 한국경제 / Hotels.com · 2026-08-31The Rakyat Post / Trip.com platform data · 2026-09-04
Regional access is changing the accommodation catchment. Gimhae marginally overtook Incheon as the entry point for Taiwanese visitors in July, with shares of 36.9% and 36.3%. New Kobe–Incheon service and restored Kitakyushu–Taipei flights add options outside familiar gateways. This makes neighbourhood readiness commercially relevant, but flights can carry residents and connecting passengers: capacity creates an opportunity to compete for nights, not proof of additional Airbnb demand. 뉴스트래블 citing Korea Tourism Organization Taipei office · 2026-09-02TRAICY · 2026-09-01TRAICY Global · 2026-09-02
Autumn demand and transport supply are not moving in lockstep. China’s holiday-window domestic air bookings were reported up about 17% year on year, while OAG puts September Indian seats down 4.5%. Within Southeast Asia, Vietnam’s departing capacity rises 10%, but Malaysia and the Philippines contract. Timing and geography matter more than a generic recovery narrative. Strong platform spending can coexist with tighter seats and higher trip costs; monthly schedules are forward supply, not realised passenger traffic. 新浪新闻（转载第一财经、界面等） · 2026-09-05OAG · 2026-09-03OAG · 2026-09-03
Platforms are competing on the total trip, including constraints. Japan’s hotel, package and airline promotions overlap, while Air India–IHG links flight loyalty with hotel stays. Fujiyoshida’s Uber partnership instead tackles pickup locations and visitor conduct. Price, rewards and on-the-ground certainty all influence conversion. Airbnb should distinguish the mechanism before responding: a coupon needs a value comparison; congestion needs operational guidance; a reported visa change needs accurate eligibility information rather than an indiscriminate discount. Rakuten Group · 2026-09-01 Uber Japan · 2026-09-04 Travel Watch · 2026-09-01Travel Trade Journal · 2026-09-04

💡 Airbnb APAC Implications

Build short-break value around the whole group. Test two-to-three-night, easy-arrival homes for Korea-origin autumn trips, showing total group cost and specific comforts rather than claiming that homes are automatically cheaper than premium hotels. Measure conversion, cancellation and total paid per guest against comparable stays. The search evidence supports a hypothesis about compressed trips and quality, not a licence to forecast Airbnb bookings. 한국경제 / Hotels.com · 2026-08-31 호텔앤레스토랑 / HotelsCombined · 2026-09-04
Prioritise a small set of regional corridors, not blanket expansion. Review legally eligible supply, language coverage, self check-in and airport instructions around Busan, Kobe and northern Kyushu. Route-specific demand should decide where acquisition investment follows. Separate guest origin, airport entry and final destination in analysis; a gateway share shift alone cannot identify the neighbourhoods where incremental stays will land. 뉴스트래블 citing Korea Tourism Organization Taipei office · 2026-09-02TRAICY · 2026-09-01TRAICY Global · 2026-09-02
Translate China’s domestic behaviour into outbound hypotheses only. Meituan’s family stays and Fliggy’s room-night growth describe domestic activity. Airbnb’s relevant commercial question is whether China-origin guests carry those preferences into Japan and Southeast Asia: group space, slower itineraries and local experiences. Validate with outbound funnel and stay-length data before reallocating spend. Do not describe Chinese domestic accommodation figures as Airbnb’s addressable domestic business. 新华网 / 美团数据 · 2026-09-03 新华网 · 2026-08-31
Protect long-stay clarity and event-period trust. Reports say Thailand’s visa-exempt allowance falls to 30 days from September 15 for affected passports. Verify current official entry rules before guest-facing guidance and distinguish immigration permission from accommodation legality. Delhi’s summit pricing separately calls for transparent totals and dependable host calendars. Neither a policy headline nor hotel scarcity justifies promising unrestricted stays or assuming displaced delegates will choose homes. The Straits Times / The Nation Asia News Network · 2026-09-02The Hindu BusinessLine · 2026-09-04

🏢 Competitor & Platform Watch

Rakuten and Yahoo sharpen the effective-price comparison. Rakuten’s domestic campaign advertises more than 20,000 lodging offers and up to 35% off first app bookings; Yahoo’s packages advertise coupons up to ¥30,000 and PayPay rewards. Korea-facing Rakuten offers have different dates and eligibility. These are maximum promotional terms, not realised savings or market-wide price falls. Monitor eligible basket prices and the friction of redeeming rewards, rather than comparing headline discounts. Rakuten Group · 2026-09-01 Travel Watch · 2026-09-01BusinessKorea / Rakuten Travel Korea · 2026-09-02
Scapia and Air India–IHG aim to capture the next booking. The Axis–Scapia card combines zero forex markup with up to 20% Scapia Coins on eligible bookings. Air India–IHG offers triple Maharaja Points on qualifying stays from September 15 through December 31. Both attach retention to transactions beyond the room search. Redemption rules and traveller overlap will determine their impact; neither announcement demonstrates a share shift away from Airbnb. ETTravelWorld · 2026-09-04 Travel Trade Journal · 2026-09-04
KATA’s committee is an early policy signal, not a new law. The Korean trade association’s standing fair-cooperation committee brings foreign-OTA conduct, registration parity and consumer protection onto its agenda. That could shape consultation and enforcement priorities, but the collected record does not establish enacted obligations. Maintain a watch on concrete proposals and local supplier responsibilities; distinguish industry advocacy from government decisions when briefing hosts or leadership. TTL뉴스 / Korea Association of Travel Agents · 2026-08-31
Klook and Uber show two forms of destination partnership. The Philippine tourism department’s MOU with Klook and Newport World Resorts concerns domestic and entertainment promotion; Uber’s Fujiyoshida agreement specifies pickup guidance, local rules and congestion information. The former is a distribution commitment, the latter an operating intervention. Neither includes measured outcomes in this pool. Airbnb should evaluate partnerships against incremental nights and neighbourhood friction, not announcement volume. Philippine News Agency · 2026-09-01Uber Japan · 2026-09-04

🇮🇳 India (भारत)

Executive summary
  • Event pressure is concentrated, not nationwide. BusinessLine cites Delhi five-star searches up 50% and hotel bookings up 25% year on year around BRICS. Treat the premium-city spike as a dated occasion, not a national accommodation growth rate. The Hindu BusinessLine · 2026-09-04
  • Domestic demand is drawing branded supply outward. Mint describes chains entering smaller destinations; Hilton reports 60 hotels under construction and commitments for another 400. Those pipeline stages are not equivalent to rooms available today, but they raise the future competitive bar. Mint · 2026-09-01 Business Standard · 2026-09-03
  • Outbound substitution meets constrained air supply. Industry commentary points travellers toward shorter, more affordable regional trips, while OAG’s September schedule totals 22.7 million seats, down 4.5% year on year. New routes do not negate a contracting national total. The Economic Times · 2026-09-04 OAG · 2026-09-03
Supporting detail
Inbound recovery remains a separate problem. FAITH’s 8–9 million foreign-visitor outlook is an industry forecast reported by Economic Times, not a final arrivals count. It sits alongside robust domestic investment rather than contradicting it. Keep inbound and domestic assumptions separate when sizing destination opportunities; neither foreign-arrival weakness nor hotel construction alone settles home demand. The Economic Times · 2026-09-06
Central Asia gains both access and distribution. The Uzbekistan visa-free announcement and Centrum Air’s planned twice-weekly Hyderabad–Tashkent launch on September 28 remove different frictions: permission and nonstop access. Air India’s Ahmedabad Easy Connect instead improves transfers to 26 international destinations through Delhi. These are corridor-specific changes, not evidence that every outbound segment is accelerating. Travel Trade Journal · 2026-09-02 ETTravelWorld · 2026-08-31 Travel Trade Journal · 2026-09-01
Loyalty makes the accommodation choice less independent. Scapia’s travel rewards and Air India–IHG’s cross-loyalty offer can influence where a traveller starts the next booking. Airbnb should compare the complete value proposition for families and groups while watching actual redemption and retention. Announced benefits establish competitive intent; the collection contains no adoption data or measured effect on accommodation market share. ETTravelWorld · 2026-09-04 Travel Trade Journal · 2026-09-04

🇰🇷 Korea (대한민국)

Executive summary
  • Chuseok planning favours compact, comfortable breaks. Hotels.com’s search mix puts roughly 60% of trips at two or three nights and more than 60% of searched nights in four- and five-star properties. Search intentions remain upstream of completed stays. 한국경제 / Hotels.com · 2026-08-31
  • Outbound interest is rising within a second platform sample. HotelsCombined reports overseas hotel searches increasing from 37% to 60% of its holiday mix. That is a share change, not 60% growth, and must not be merged with Hotels.com into one dataset. 호텔앤레스토랑 / HotelsCombined · 2026-09-04
  • Busan is gaining Taiwan-facing gateway relevance. Gimhae handled 36.9% of July Taiwanese arrivals, just above Incheon’s 36.3%. The reported 900 Taipei–Gimhae flights help explain access, but visitor destination and length of stay still need validation. 뉴스트래블 citing Korea Tourism Organization Taipei office · 2026-09-02
Supporting detail
Aviation depth and Japan promotions reinforce one corridor. September schedule reporting highlights Incheon–Narita’s international seat ranking, while Rakuten markets Japan lodging discounts to Korean customers. Availability and promotion can reduce trip-planning friction together. The commercial question is conversion into a short, reliable itinerary; neither a route ranking nor a maximum coupon measures the demand captured by independent accommodation. 항공여행 · 2026-09-02 BusinessKorea / Rakuten Travel Korea · 2026-09-02
Workation is product positioning, not proof of a boom. KTO’s English-language guide presents communities, remote-work appeal and visa options. That supports checking workspace quality, connectivity and longer-stay readiness in eligible homes. It does not demonstrate a new visa rule this week or quantify remote-worker arrivals. Avoid presenting promotional destination content as either enacted reform or observed growth. VISITKOREA / Korea Tourism Organization · 2026-09-02
Platform-policy advocacy deserves a concrete watchlist. KATA’s committee raises registration and consumer-protection parity, alongside inbound guide qualifications. Follow published proposals and enforcement decisions rather than extrapolating a ban or opening from a trade-association launch. The missing official policy release and unavailable Naver backup constrain confidence about the complete regulatory picture this week. TTL뉴스 / Korea Association of Travel Agents · 2026-08-31

🇯🇵 Japan (日本)

Executive summary
  • Autumn planning is an active competitive battleground. Rakuten’s 28-day sale and Yahoo’s air-plus-hotel promotion target the booking window with different mechanics. Compare eligible total prices, not advertised ceilings; promotions alone do not prove weak demand. Rakuten Group · 2026-09-01 Travel Watch · 2026-09-01
  • New gateways widen options around Kansai. Asiana launched daily Kobe–Incheon service on September 1, scheduled through March 27, 2027. It adds Korean access and network connections, but additional seats are not yet evidence of additional local overnight stays. TRAICY · 2026-09-01
  • Visitor-flow management is becoming a platform function. Uber and Fujiyoshida will use designated pickup guidance, etiquette messaging and restriction information around Fuji tourism areas. The practical implication is better arrival coordination, not an assumption that congestion is already solved. Uber Japan · 2026-09-04
Supporting detail
Hotel assets are being repackaged for drive tourism. Ooedo-Onsen Monogatari opened reservation-only RV stays at seven properties from ¥3,500 per vehicle-night, using existing bathing, dining and staffed facilities. This competes through predictable amenities rather than conventional room inventory. Airbnb can learn from the clarity of the proposition without inferring a measured camper-demand surge from one operator’s launch. Travel Watch · 2026-09-03
Fare sales and local incentives lower different barriers. Peach’s sale offers selected one-way fares from ¥4,000 for travel beginning September 28, while regional campaigns and Gifu lodging-only hometown-tax coupons reduce costs at destination. Eligibility and availability vary. Connecting suitable homes to accessible regional itineraries is a testable idea; aggregating these offers into a nationwide subsidy or average saving would be misleading. Travel Watch · 2026-09-02 Travel Watch · 2026-09-04 Nippon Air Transport via PR Times · 2026-09-04
Seasonality needs evidence beyond campaign calendars. Nikkei describes heat and foreign visitors shifting peak earnings toward autumn, but its original page was unavailable to the collector. Use that as a directional interpretation alongside verified promotions, not a quantified forecast. Trip.com’s forthcoming Tourism EXPO presence adds trade visibility; it provides no independent consumer demand or booking-performance measure. Nikkei Asia · 2026-09-02 Trip.com International Travel Japan via PR Times · 2026-09-03

🇨🇳 China (中国)

Executive summary
  • Family travel is leaning into time at destination. Meituan’s summer observation, reported by Xinhua, identifies four-to-five-day stays as common among families and rising county-level interest. These are platform observations about domestic behaviour, not a representative national stay-length estimate. 新华网 / 美团数据 · 2026-09-03
  • Fliggy reports substantial domestic room-night growth. The platform says summer hotel room nights rose 66% year on year and attraction tickets nearly 30%. Platform scope and season matter: do not translate this into national hotel growth or Airbnb performance. 新华网 · 2026-08-31
  • Cheap shoulder-season fares coexist with holiday advance demand. Reported September 25–October 7 air bookings exceed 3.83 million domestic and 1.77 million cross-border tickets, up about 17% and 11%. Those are booking snapshots as of September 4, not final passenger totals. 新浪新闻（转载第一财经、界面等） · 2026-09-05
Supporting detail
Summer aviation provides scale, with different denominators. The 62-day transport season recorded 151 million civil-aviation passenger journeys. A separate July 1–August 25 window counted over 7.06 million inbound-route passengers. Neither is a count of unique tourists, and inbound-route passengers need not all be foreign visitors. Their useful role is contextualising access and seasonal concentration, not sizing Airbnb bookings. 新华网 / 航旅纵横 · 2026-09-03
Shanghai is adding reasons to visit in autumn. The tourism festival’s programme includes more than 170 cultural and tourism activities across food, night visits and slower exploration. The mechanism is occasion-led itinerary formation; the release does not quantify incremental nights. For China-origin outbound merchandising, use the preference for participation as a hypothesis, while keeping Shanghai’s domestic programme outside direct Airbnb inventory claims. 新华社 · 2026-09-04
Forward hotel interest is not the same as realised occupancy. Qunar’s reported popular-city holiday advance bookings rise nearly 40%, alongside a 21% increase in interest in booking air travel a month ahead. These measures support monitoring lead times and price sensitivity, but cannot be added to Fliggy room nights or national passenger counts. The Tianjin expo is a supply-side industry event, not additional consumer demand evidence. 北京日报客户端 · 2026-08-31 新华丝路 · 2026-09-04

🌴 Southeast Asia

Executive summary
  • Vietnam leads the selected capacity comparison. OAG’s September departing seats rise 10% to 7.3 million, while Singapore rises 3.4% to 3.7 million. Malaysia and the Philippines decline 6.5% and 5.7%; this is an uneven supply outlook, not one regional recovery rate. OAG · 2026-09-03
  • Malaysia’s platform spending signal is strong but selective. Trip.com reports triple-digit H1 growth in flight and hotel spending and nearly quadrupled attraction bookings. A platform’s expansion and customer mix can amplify growth; these figures do not establish equivalent nationwide tourism spending gains. The Rakyat Post / Trip.com platform data · 2026-09-04
  • Thailand’s reported stay-limit change matters most for longer trips. The September 15 reduction from 60 to 30 visa-exempt days affects specified passports, including Singapore and Malaysia. Typical short breaks and longer stays face different exposure; official rules must be checked before traveller guidance. The Straits Times / The Nation Asia News Network · 2026-09-02
Supporting detail
Vietnam combines a holiday pulse with new connectivity. VNAT-attributed reporting estimates 6.5 million tourists over the August 29–September 2 National Day holiday, up 18.1%. Tourism Malaysia separately confirms daily Phu Quoc–Kuala Lumpur service from September 1. The former is an observed holiday estimate; the latter an access change. Test whether corridor demand supports suitable local stays rather than treating both as additive visitors. VietnamPlus (Vietnam News Agency), citing VNAT · 2026-09-03 Tourism Malaysia · 2026-09-01
Philippine operators are adapting to affordability pressure. PHILTOA describes a shift toward lower-cost land packages and nearby ASEAN markets as airfares rise. DOT’s 6.4–6.8 million arrivals goal, with seven million as a stretch, remains a target rather than achieved performance. Limited original-page extraction means the briefing cannot quantify the substitution or identify winners beyond the retained excerpts. Context.ph, citing Philippines Department of Tourism · 2026-09-01 Context.ph, citing PHILTOA · 2026-09-05
Activities distribution is expanding through partnerships. DOT’s Klook and Newport World Resorts MOU links domestic and entertainment promotion, while Travel Mart provides a consumer and trade activation. Both can help turn occasions into bookable products, but the source pool has no conversion results. Singapore-specific evidence is especially thin beyond schedules and Thailand policy; do not generalise Malaysian platform behaviour to Singapore. Philippine News Agency · 2026-09-01 Discover MNL / PHILTOA · 2026-09-03

🇭🇰🇹🇼 Hong Kong & Taiwan

Executive summary
  • Hong Kong gets a narrow new Mainland feeder. Hong Kong Airlines’ twice-weekly Urumqi service launched August 29 and was reported September 1. It adds a northwest-China connection and potential hub transfers; the record does not identify incremental Hong Kong overnight visitors. TRAICY Global · 2026-09-01
  • Premium cross-border mobility is being reshaped. EAA suspended most scheduled helicopter services from September 1, retaining Macau–Shenzhen scheduled flights and shifting other activity to charters. The operator cites heliport relocation and market changes, not a measured collapse in regional tourism. HK01 · 2026-09-02
  • Taiwan’s Japan access is rebuilding selectively. StarFlyer resumed Kitakyushu–Taoyuan on September 2 with three weekly round trips after a March 2020 suspension. Future frequency expansion is an ambition while demand is tested, not a committed capacity total. TRAICY Global · 2026-09-02
Supporting detail
Taiwan is targeting Malaysia through repeat and group travel. Coverage of the Tourism Administration’s MATTA Fair activity describes repeat-visitor and MICE/accommodation incentives, plus a Malaysia Airlines MOU for product development and joint marketing. The mechanism is coordinated source-market activation. The retained report is a secondary lifestyle/trade account, not an official terms document; do not promise incentive amounts, eligibility or measured uptake from it. Malaysian Foodie · 2026-09-05
Separate new access from the case for new supply. The Urumqi and northern-Kyushu routes connect distinct traveller pools and operate at modest frequencies. Review existing legal listing availability and transport guidance before inferring a need to acquire broadly across either market. Resident travel, connections and business trips may absorb seats without creating the same independent-accommodation demand as leisure overnight visitors. TRAICY Global · 2026-09-01 TRAICY Global · 2026-09-02
The evidence supports a corridor watch, not a market forecast. Four dated records meet the numerical richness floor, but three concern aviation and the fourth promotion. There is no retained direct consumer-search or booking series, and no first-party Taiwan incentive publication. Keep this section deliberately bounded: monitor destination-level nights and programme terms before claiming broad growth, price strength or an Airbnb share opportunity. HK01 · 2026-09-02 Malaysian Foodie · 2026-09-05

📅 Upcoming Travel Windows

September planning checkpoints. September 10–12: IATO convention in Visakhapatnam. September 15: reported Thailand entry-rule change and start of Air India–IHG promotional stays. September 24–27: Chuseok search window and Tourism EXPO Japan. September 28: planned Hyderabad–Tashkent launch and beginning of Peach’s eligible travel period. These are sourced commercial and planning dates, not a complete public-holiday calendar. 📋 Sources Audit

Verified input coverage: 6/6; shared upstream failure: none. Gate-approved dated records: India 20; Korea 9; Japan 10; China 7; Southeast Asia 10; Hong Kong/Taiwan 4; total 60. These are collection records, not 60 independent studies: India has two entries from one Aviation Week URL (59 distinct URLs overall), two Delhi stories covering the same event, and Rakuten coverage overlaps across markets. China has ten raw candidates but only seven gate-approved records; the other three are not used here.

Coverage is publication August 31–September 6, 2026; observation periods can be earlier or future. All six markets reach four dated records, but HK/TW only just does. Company claims, forecasts, schedules, searches, journeys and completed stays are explicitly distinguished.

item.title: Jul 27–Aug 2, 2026: Japan decouples — fewer visitors, record spend, and zero-day STR bans
item.itunes:author: Max (ZQ's AI Agent)
item.description:
Asia Travel Weekly — Jul 27–Aug 2, 2026 (Week 31)
== KEY SIGNALS == • Japan decouples volume from value: Q2 inbound spend held a record ¥2,509.6B (~$16.2B, +0.2% YoY) even as arrivals fell 5.3% to 10.4M — the first quarterly decline of the post-COVID recovery. Per-capita spend +3.3%, and the US overtook China as Japan's largest spending market for the first time as Chinese arrivals fell 58.2%. • Asia's boom becomes an affordability problem: Seoul hotel ADR +59.7% YoY to ₩161,609 (~$116), Busan +30.8%, Jeju +21.3%; Korean analysts blame tightened STR regulation for the missing alternative supply. In Japan, 90.3% of overnight travellers call lodging expensive and 31.9% of plan-revisers replaced a hotel night with an overnight bus. • Japan's Tourism Agency green-lights outright municipal STR bans — ordinances may cut minpaku operating days from 180 to as low as zero, plus mandatory ICT remote management. Shibuya's revised ordinance (effective Jul 1) leaves ~63 operable days a year in restricted zones. • China runs record volume at falling prices: rail carried 432M passengers in 31 summer days (1.01B projected, +7.1%), aviation heads for a record July, yet average domestic economy fare fell to ¥834.7 (~$116) — the lowest July since the pandemic.
== AIRBNB APAC IMPLICATIONS == • Korea's ADR shock is the clearest affordability opening in years, but a new disaster-liability insurance mandate hits ~12,000 STR properties alongside the 15.5% host-only fee — pair the demand story with concrete host-cost guidance. • Japan's zero-day rule changes the planning unit from city to ward: build ordinance early-warning across the top 30 municipalities by listing concentration, and lean supply toward regions courting visitors (Hokkaido/Okinawa Obon above last year; furusato-nozei travel vouchers). • The lodging-price backlash leaks demand out of the category entirely — make value legible (total price, per-head group cost, multi-night discounts) in the JP/KR funnels this season. • SEA is where volume and price both still work: HCMC intl +42.7% to 7.1M, Hanoi intl +25%, Malaysia 21.12M H1 vs a 47M VM2026 target. Accor is committing ~3,750 luxury rooms to VN/TH/ID. • China's distribution map is being rewritten: Meituan's assistant moved from answering to transacting, while Trip.com shut the merchant traffic-control tool at the centre of the antitrust case and conceded a profit hit.
== MARKETS == • India — IndiGo ends all widebody damp-lease long-haul from Oct 25 (London, Manchester, Copenhagen, Amsterdam), handing India–Europe back to Air India; Cleartrip targets early-2027 breakeven against MakeMyTrip's FY26 $10.4B gross bookings; airport-hotel land grab accelerates. • Korea — 10M+ H1 inbound but ADR +59.7%; Yanolja and Yeogi Eottae indicted over expired-coupon forfeitures (~$27M alleged harm); Yeogi Eottae closes its Relux acquisition, going Korea–Japan dual-market. • Japan — Q2 record spend on falling arrivals; JTA permits zero-day minpaku ordinances; Accor launches a ~¥39,000 (~$252) paid loyalty tier. • China — 1.8B+ summer trips projected; Aug 8–9 departures +62% MoM; inbound disperses to tier-3/4 (Zhangjiajie Grand Canyon 50%+ foreign guests); visa-free transit expansion. • SEA — Malaysia 21.12M H1; Vietnam Decree 286/2026 tightens e-visa oversight from Sep 15; Philippines 3.16M (+5.4%) with China +64% YTD, seats now the constraint. • HK/TW — Hong Kong 28M Jan–Jul (+12%), Q3 air capacity +7%, "Only in Hong Kong" brand refresh; Taiwan posts a record 6.36M travel deficit and answers with an NT$3.46B (~$106M) weekday domestic incentive that excludes OTA bookings.

Asia Travel Weekly — Jul 20–26, 2026 (Week 30)
== KEY SIGNALS == • China hands Trip.com a record ¥5.179B (~$765M) antitrust penalty — SAMR closed a six-month probe on Jul 25, ordering ¥1.658B (~$244M) forfeited gains plus a ¥3.521B (~$518M) fine, set at 7.5% of ¥46.96B 2025 mainland sales. First monopoly ruling ever against a Chinese OTA. • Northeast Asia rebalances: Korea H1 arrivals 10.7M (+21.3% YoY, +26.9% vs pre-pandemic) while Japan fell 2.0% to 21.1M — mainland Chinese arrivals down 56.4% to 2.06M, cutting China to 9.8% of Japan inbound, lowest since 2003. • Volume and spend decouple: Japan Q2 visitor spending hit ¥2.5096T (~$15.4B) despite three straight monthly arrival declines. Mexican visitors are now the highest per-capita spenders, ~40% above Americans. • Supply is being built in small cities: tier 3–5 Chinese cities account for 53.2% of net new inbound-licensed hotels vs 7.5% for tier-1; tier-4 cities already host 2.4x more inbound guests than tier-1.
== AIRBNB APAC IMPLICATIONS == • The Trip.com ruling is a regulatory read-across, not just a competitor headline — the theory of harm (partner terms, pricing conduct) is portable; expect Korea and India regulators to cite it within two quarters. • Korea is the highest-conviction supply build: policy tailwind (visa-free Chinese groups extended), demand tailwind (+21.3%), 22–23M FY target — and Airbnb's 15.5% host-only fee went live for all Korean hosts on May 25, making host repricing education time-sensitive. • Long-stay compounds fastest and is structurally ours: Tujia 7+ day stays +30%, 15+ day stays +40%; Korea's F-1-D workation visa became a permanent 3-year programme Jun 30. • Japan's minpaku drift is the key risk: the new "zero-day rule" lets municipalities ban short-term rentals outright in designated zones. New Kyoto analysis clearing Chinese visitors of primary overtourism blame is useful evidence for local engagement.
== MARKETS == • India — MakeMyTrip filed a confidential SEBI DRHP; Cleartrip targets 45% non-air revenue and break-even by early FY27; OTA market projected to reach ₹3.84T (~$458B) by FY28; Tourism Ministry sanctioned 117 projects worth ₹5,756.62cr (~$686M); IHCL revenue +14.6%. • Korea — 10.7M H1 arrivals; workation visa permanent (3 years, $5,250/month); Airbnb completes 15.5% host-only fee rollout; foreign tourists shifting to markets and hiking trails (DDP +12.1%, Mt. Acha +11.8%). • Japan — H1 −2.0%; Q2 spend ¥2.51T; departure tax tripled to ¥3,000; "zero-day rule" plus mandatory ICT host obligations; Obon peak Aug 8–16. • China — Trip.com fined; 22.91M H1 foreign arrivals (+20.4%), 77.7% visa-free; Tujia 15+ day stays +40%; Fliggy accommodation +58%; family trips ≤3 days now 52% of parent-child bookings while peak hotel prices run 70%+ above normal. • SEA — Vietnam 12.3M H1 (+14.9%), European arrivals +56.1%, HCMC MICE +35%; Malaysia 10.6M in five months vs 47M VM2026 target; Singapore 83.09% occupancy at SGD 291 ADR. • HK/Taiwan — Hong Kong 26.71M H1 (+13%), long-haul +19%, HKTB launched "Only in Hong Kong" Jul 21; Hongkongers' mainland card spend ~+30%; Taiwan spent ~$22B in Japan in Q1, second globally.
== CALENDAR == Japan Obon Aug 8–16 · Korea Liberation Day Aug 15 · India Independence Day Aug 15 · China summer peak through Aug 31 · HK/Taiwan/Philippines typhoon peak through Sep · Vietnam National Day Sep 2 · Taiwan Design Expo Sep 24–Oct 11.
